article.title: How to Install Luxury Vinyl Plank Flooring
article.summary: Install click-lock luxury vinyl plank (LVP) flooring: prep a flat subfloor, plan the layout, stagger seams, and leave the right expansion gap.
article.body:
Click-lock vinyl plank floats over most flat, solid subfloors, needs no glue, and stands up to water better than laminate. This guide covers a typical bedroom or living room. Your product's installation sheet always wins over general advice, especially on gap size and underlayment.

Affiliate disclosure: some links in this guide are affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. We only recommend products we'd use ourselves.

Safety: wear knee pads and eye protection when cutting. If you're pulling up old sheet vinyl or tile in a home built before the 1980s, don't sand or break it until it has been tested for asbestos.

Steps

  1. Prep the room and the subfloor

    Remove baseboards (number them for reinstallation), old carpet and staples. Vacuum thoroughly. Lay a long straightedge across the floor and fill dips with leveling compound. Grind or sand high spots. Click joints break over humps and hollows.

    Done right: the floor is clean, solid, and as flat as your product's tolerance requires (often about 3/16 in over 10 ft).

  2. Undercut door jambs

    Lay a plank on a scrap of underlayment against the door casing and cut the casing along its top with a jamb saw. The new floor slides underneath, giving you a clean edge without trim.

    Done right: a plank slides under the casing with a little room to spare.

  3. Plan the layout so both walls get wide boards

    Measure the room's width and divide by the plank's face width. If the last row would be narrower than half a plank, rip the first row narrower so the first and last rows match. Run planks parallel to the longest wall or toward the main light source.

    Done right: no row on either side is narrower than half a plank.

  4. Install the first row with spacers

    Trim the tongue off the long edge of the first-row planks that face the wall. Set spacers against the wall to hold the expansion gap your manufacturer specifies (commonly about 1/4 in), and click each plank's short end into the last.

    Done right: the first row is dead straight, so check it with a string line, and the gap is consistent.

  5. Stagger seams and click rows together

    Start each new row with the offcut from the previous row, as long as it's at least 8 in long and the end joints land at least 6 in from those in the row before. Angle the long edge into the previous row, lower it, and tap the short end closed with a tapping block.

    Done right: joints close fully with no gaps or lifted edges, and no seams line up into an obvious pattern.

  6. Fit the last row and tight spots

    Measure the last row at several points, subtract the expansion gap, and rip planks to width. Use the pull bar where you can't swing a mallet. Mix planks from several boxes as you go to spread out color and pattern repeats.

    Done right: the last row is snug, with the gap kept all the way around.

  7. Add transitions and reinstall trim

    Install transition strips at doorways and where the floor meets other flooring. Reinstall baseboards or add quarter round, nailing into the wall, never into the floor.

    Done right: all edges are covered, and the floor can still move freely under the trim.

Call a pro if: the subfloor is bouncy or soft, there's moisture coming up through a concrete slab, or you're laying over radiant heat. Each needs work beyond a standard floating install.

FAQ

Do I need underlayment under vinyl plank?

Only if the manufacturer allows it. Many planks have a pad already attached, and adding more can void the warranty and stress the locking joints. Over concrete, a vapor barrier may be required.

Do I need to acclimate vinyl plank flooring?

Follow your product's instructions. Many brands recommend leaving the boxes in the room for about 48 hours at normal living temperature before you install.

How big should the expansion gap be?

It depends on the product. Around 1/4 in is common for rooms of normal size, and larger rooms may need more or a transition break.

Can I install vinyl plank over tile?

Often, if the tile is solid and flat and the grout lines are shallow. Deep grout lines should be filled first.
